operations.description: Creates a storage container to hold objects. A container is similar to a bucket in the Amazon S3 service.
operations.T: [METHOD] post [NAME] create container [PATH] x amz target media store 20170901 create container [PARAMS] 256 algorithm amz content credential date headers security sha signature signed target token x [SCHEMA] access arn container create enabled endpoint exceeded exception input key limit list logging output stamp status tag time value

operations.description: Deletes the specified container. Before you make a DeleteContainer request, delete any objects in the container or in any folders in the container. You can delete only empty containers.
operations.T: [METHOD] post [NAME] delete container [PATH] x amz target media store 20170901 delete container [PARAMS] 256 algorithm amz content credential date headers security sha signature signed target token x [SCHEMA] container delete input output

operations.description: Deletes the access policy that is associated with the specified container.
operations.T: [METHOD] post [NAME] delete container policy [PATH] x amz target media store 20170901 delete container policy [PARAMS] 256 algorithm amz content credential date headers security sha signature signed target token x [SCHEMA] container delete exception found input not output policy

operations.description:
Deletes the cross-origin resource sharing (CORS) configuration information that is set for the container.

To use this operation, you must have permission to perform the MediaStore:DeleteCorsPolicy action. The container owner has this permission by default and can grant this permission to others.
operations.T: [METHOD] post [NAME] delete cors policy [PATH] x amz target media store 20170901 delete cors policy [PARAMS] 256 algorithm amz content credential date headers security sha signature signed target token x [SCHEMA] cors delete exception found input not output policy

operations.description: Removes an object lifecycle policy from a container. It takes up to 20 minutes for the change to take effect.
operations.T: [METHOD] post [NAME] delete lifecycle policy [PATH] x amz target media store 20170901 delete lifecycle policy [PARAMS] 256 algorithm amz content credential date headers security sha signature signed target token x [SCHEMA] delete exception found input lifecycle not output policy

operations.description: Retrieves the properties of the requested container. This request is commonly used to retrieve the endpoint of a container. An endpoint is a value assigned by the service when a new container is created. A container's endpoint does not change after it has been assigned. The DescribeContainer request returns a single Container object based on ContainerName. To return all Container objects that are associated with a specified AWS account, use ListContainers.
operations.T: [METHOD] post [NAME] describe container [PATH] x amz target media store 20170901 describe container [PARAMS] 256 algorithm amz content credential date headers security sha signature signed target token x [SCHEMA] access arn container describe enabled endpoint input logging output stamp status time

operations.description: Retrieves the access policy for the specified container. For information about the data that is included in an access policy, see the AWS Identity and Access Management User Guide.
operations.T: [METHOD] post [NAME] container policy [PATH] x amz target media store 20170901 container policy [PARAMS] 256 algorithm amz content credential date headers security sha signature signed target token x [SCHEMA] container exception found input not output policy

operations.description:
Returns the cross-origin resource sharing (CORS) configuration information that is set for the container.

To use this operation, you must have permission to perform the MediaStore:GetCorsPolicy action. By default, the container owner has this permission and can grant it to others.
operations.T: [METHOD] post [NAME] cors policy [PATH] x amz target media store 20170901 cors policy [PARAMS] 256 algorithm amz content credential date headers security sha signature signed target token x [SCHEMA] age allowed cors exception expose found headers input max methods not origins output policy rule seconds

operations.description: Retrieves the object lifecycle policy that is assigned to a container.
operations.T: [METHOD] post [NAME] lifecycle policy [PATH] x amz target media store 20170901 lifecycle policy [PARAMS] 256 algorithm amz content credential date headers security sha signature signed target token x [SCHEMA] exception found input lifecycle not output policy

operations.description:
Lists the properties of all containers in AWS Elemental MediaStore.

You can query to receive all the containers in one response. Or you can include the MaxResults parameter to receive a limited number of containers in each response. In this case, the response includes a token. To get the next set of containers, send the command again, this time with the NextToken parameter (with the returned token as its value). The next set of responses appears, with a token if there are still more containers to receive.

See also DescribeContainer, which gets the properties of one container.
operations.T: [METHOD] post [NAME] list containers [PATH] x amz target media store 20170901 list containers [PARAMS] 256 algorithm amz content credential date headers max next results security sha signature signed target token x [SCHEMA] access arn container containers enabled endpoint input limit list logging output pagination stamp status time token

operations.description: Returns a list of the tags assigned to the specified container.
operations.T: [METHOD] post [NAME] list tags for resource [PATH] x amz target media store 20170901 list tags for resource [PARAMS] 256 algorithm amz content credential date headers security sha signature signed target token x [SCHEMA] arn container for input key list output resource tag tags value

operations.description:
Creates an access policy for the specified container to restrict the users and clients that can access it. For information about the data that is included in an access policy, see the AWS Identity and Access Management User Guide.

For this release of the REST API, you can create only one policy for a container. If you enter PutContainerPolicy twice, the second command modifies the existing policy.
operations.T: [METHOD] post [NAME] put container policy [PATH] x amz target media store 20170901 put container policy [PARAMS] 256 algorithm amz content credential date headers security sha signature signed target token x [SCHEMA] container input output policy put

operations.description:
Sets the cross-origin resource sharing (CORS) configuration on a container so that the container can service cross-origin requests. For example, you might want to enable a request whose origin is http://www.example.com to access your AWS Elemental MediaStore container at my.example.container.com by using the browser's XMLHttpRequest capability.

To enable CORS on a container, you attach a CORS policy to the container. In the CORS policy, you configure rules that identify origins and the HTTP methods that can be executed on your container. The policy can contain up to 398,000 characters. You can add up to 100 rules to a CORS policy. If more than one rule applies, the service uses the first applicable rule listed.

To learn more about CORS, see Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) in AWS Elemental MediaStore.
operations.T: [METHOD] post [NAME] put cors policy [PATH] x amz target media store 20170901 put cors policy [PARAMS] 256 algorithm amz content credential date headers security sha signature signed target token x [SCHEMA] age allowed cors expose headers input max methods origins output policy put rule seconds

operations.description:
Writes an object lifecycle policy to a container. If the container already has an object lifecycle policy, the service replaces the existing policy with the new policy. It takes up to 20 minutes for the change to take effect.

For information about how to construct an object lifecycle policy, see Components of an Object Lifecycle Policy.
operations.T: [METHOD] post [NAME] put lifecycle policy [PATH] x amz target media store 20170901 put lifecycle policy [PARAMS] 256 algorithm amz content credential date headers security sha signature signed target token x [SCHEMA] input lifecycle output policy put

operations.description: Starts access logging on the specified container. When you enable access logging on a container, MediaStore delivers access logs for objects stored in that container to Amazon CloudWatch Logs.
operations.T: [METHOD] post [NAME] start access logging [PATH] x amz target media store 20170901 start access logging [PARAMS] 256 algorithm amz content credential date headers security sha signature signed target token x [SCHEMA] access input logging output start

operations.description: Stops access logging on the specified container. When you stop access logging on a container, MediaStore stops sending access logs to Amazon CloudWatch Logs. These access logs are not saved and are not retrievable.
operations.T: [METHOD] post [NAME] stop access logging [PATH] x amz target media store 20170901 stop access logging [PARAMS] 256 algorithm amz content credential date headers security sha signature signed target token x [SCHEMA] access input logging output stop

operations.description: Adds tags to the specified AWS Elemental MediaStore container. Tags are key:value pairs that you can associate with AWS resources. For example, the tag key might be "customer" and the tag value might be "companyA." You can specify one or more tags to add to each container. You can add up to 50 tags to each container. For more information about tagging, including naming and usage conventions, see Tagging Resources in MediaStore.
operations.T: [METHOD] post [NAME] tag resource [PATH] x amz target media store 20170901 tag resource [PARAMS] 256 algorithm amz content credential date headers security sha signature signed target token x [SCHEMA] arn container input key list output resource tag value

operations.description: Removes tags from the specified container. You can specify one or more tags to remove.
operations.T: [METHOD] post [NAME] untag resource [PATH] x amz target media store 20170901 untag resource [PARAMS] 256 algorithm amz content credential date headers security sha signature signed target token x [SCHEMA] arn container input key list output resource tag untag
